evidence.assay_type: Ear swelling measurement in a rat ACD model
evidence.experimental_conditions: Female Lewis rats sensitized with oxazolone; challenged 7 days later by application of 0.5% oxazolone onto the ear; ear swelling measured at 24 hours post-challenge.
evidence.support_text: In a rat model of allergic contact dermatitis, oxazolone challenge induced ear swelling; the control (oxazolone-only) group served as the baseline, and Kv1.3 blockers reduced this swelling dose-dependently. evidence.assay_type: MEST (mouse ear swelling test, contact hypersensitivity)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Sensitization: 10% oxazolone in acetone or alcohol painted on shaved abdomen for 3 days. Challenge: 1% oxazolone in olive oil painted on left ear; ear thickness measured 24 h later with a micrometer. Mice: Ash CS1 strain. Positive response threshold: ear thickness ≥ 275 U (1 U = 10⁻⁴ cm).
evidence.support_text: In group A experiments, mice were skin-sensitized by painting the shaved abdomen for 3 days with 10% oxazolone (4-ethoxymethylene-2-phenyloxazolone) in acetone or alcohol. Skin challenge was performed by painting the left ear with 1% oxazolone in olive oil; ear thickness was measured 24 h later. Preliminary studies established that challenged unsensitized Ash CS1 mice gave ear thickness ≤250 U, while challenged skin-sensitized mice gave ear thickness >300 U (usually 325+), with a borderline of 275 U (1 U = 10⁻⁴ cm) for positive versus negative responses.
